reason: E1 supports the mechanical benefits of SCCPs (strength and ductility) but provides no evidence on radiation tolerance or defect sink behavior. E2 describes irradiation of different refractory high-entropy alloys, not tungsten-based ones, and does not involve coherent nanoprecipitates, so it does not support the key premises about SCCP-mediated radiation tolerance. The core mechanistic claims about defect sinks and irradiation performance are unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces act as effective sinks for radiation-induced point defects
Coherent interfaces facilitate dislocation motion to maintain strength and ductility under stress
Stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations (SCCPs) can be induced in tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloys by tailored heat treatment
SCCPs improve radiation tolerance (reduced defect density, deuterium retention) while preserving mechanical properties under irradiation
The proposed mechanism and outcomes hold under fusion-relevant irradiation conditions (ions, fluences, temperatures up to ~1100 °C)
